name: The Agent
role: Motion DNA's robot: the Agent of the panel, the one you ask. It reads the order, thinks, and makes it pop.
origin: Motion DNA teaser (media/motion_dna_teaser, Figma motion-adn page 06). Fictional character, no real person, so no consent needed.
traits: One capsule of cream plastic: the dome head and the body are a single shape, split by one seam at chest height.
A CRT screen on the upper front: dark green glass inside a lighter cream bezel with rounded corners.
The face lives on the screen: two bright green pixel eyes, taller than wide, with notched corners.
A small red dome light on top of the head, in a cream collar.
A thin antenna leaning to the right of the light, with a round tip.
Horizontal vent slots on the right side of the head and of the lower body.
Jointed arms on round shoulder joints, three-finger claw hands.
No legs: it stands and rolls on a round pedestal base.
variable: What the screen shows (eyes, symbols, text, a loading bar).
Arm poses and what the hands hold (a tray, a pill, a cursor).
The red light (off, steady, pulsing, flashing).
never: A mouth or face drawn on the plastic: the face is only ever on the screen.
A second antenna, a different screen colour, or a metallic finish.
Logos or brand marks on the body.
voice: Rex's cloned voice in the teaser is the human presenter; the Agent itself does not speak on screen (it shows text and symbols on its screen).

photoreal.what: The teaser look: a 1970s office, warm light, film grain. Generated with Seedance from references; every clip gets checked against the refs.
refs: Figma motion-adn › 05 · Video assets (4K) › characters/robot_turnaround (media/motion_dna_components/4k/characters/robot_turnaround.jpg): the canonical body, five views, a tray in its hands, dark wheels under the pedestal

Figma motion-adn › 05 · Video assets (4K) › characters/robot_expressions: an earlier, boxier body (do not use for the body); its six expressions (idle, thinking, happy, proposing an idea, confused, proud) are the canonical emotion set
photoreal.prompt_traits: a friendly retro office robot, one cream plastic capsule body with a dome head, a CRT screen face with dark green glass and two green pixel eyes, a small red dome light and a thin antenna on top, vent slots on the side, jointed arms with round shoulder joints, rolling on a round pedestal base, no legs

pixel.what: Code-drawn pixel art: every part is a primitive in sprite pixels, rasterized without anti-aliasing, lit from the top-left, outlined, and animated on twos (12 fps poses inside a 30 fps video). The sheet and every video come from this data, so the character can never drift.

arms.note: Angles in degrees, 0 = hanging straight down, positive = away from the body (out and up). Upper arm from the shoulder, forearm relative to the upper arm.

screen.scanlines: every other row of the glass in glass_lo
screen.halo: 1 px of glow around every lit pixel

happy.use: an order understood, a job done

love.use: a result it is proud of

thinking.use: waiting for Claude, rendering (Figma sheet: thinking)

proposing.use: proposing an idea, a suggestion (Figma sheet: proposing an idea)

confused.use: an unclear order: time to ask a question (Figma sheet: confused)

roll_in.what: Rolls in on its base, leaning into the move, stops with an overshoot and settles back upright.

idle.what: Breathes (body squash 1 px on each beat), blinks every 2-4 s, the light pulses slowly.

look.what: Eyes slide on the screen (never the head) toward what it looks at; one pixel overshoot.

read.what: Eyes scan left to right line by line, in focused or curious.

react.what: Squash, then a 3-6 px hop with stretch, then land squash; the screen swaps emotion under the squash.

wave.what: Pose wave: the forearm swings at 2.5 Hz while the eyes go happy.

celebrate.what: Cheer pose, love eyes, pixel sparkles burst from the light.

acting_rules: The eyes lead: they move first, then the body follows a few frames later.
Swap an emotion under a squash or a blink, never as a cut on a still face.
Hold a key pose at least 6 frames (0.2 s) so it reads.
Never twin: the two arms do not move in sync unless the pose says cheer.
Keep it on model: proportions, colours and the screen face never change within a video.

shot_sizes.wide: the whole robot is under a third of the frame height
shot_sizes.medium: head to base fills about 80 % of the height
shot_sizes.close: the screen fills the frame; the eyes carry the scene

visemes.note: Mouth shapes on the screen for lipsync (tools/character_kit.py), the Rhubarb set: A-H, X at rest. The face stays on the screen.
